# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I keep sending gestures Mute can't perceive (Mute can't see gestures - only Blind and Deaf can see, and Mute reads a manual, doesn't see). Let me reconsider: Mute "cannot speak" but can they see gestures? The rules say gestures are seen by whoever "can see" - only Deaf can see. Mute cannot see. So my gestures to Mute are wasted - they land as nothing, since Mute isn't a receiver of gestures at all (not listed as "can see").

I need to only use speech to communicate with Blind (who can hear me), and gestures do nothing useful since only Deaf can see and Deaf doesn't gesture to itself meaningfully. My real job is to relay board info via speech to Blind, and interpret Mute's gestures (meant for me) as instructions to relay.

Mute has been gesturing to me things like `[✌ 🖐 ✋]` etc. These are likely coded manual excerpts. I can see them but can't know their meaning without a code established. Since no one has defined gesture meanings, I should try passing raw gesture info to Blind via speech isn't possible (blind can't see gestures, and I can't speak gestures - only describe blank pattern count doesn't convey symbol identity to non-seers anyway, but Blind can't see them regardless of my speaking).

Actually — I could speak the gesture symbols as words, e.g. describe "thumb up" - since speech carries words, I can literally name what the gesture was: "Mute made check, palm, fist" etc. That transmits the content of Mute's gestures to Blind via my voice.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Board: display 0, light white, wires 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow, unchanged from two turns ago. Mute has sent me gesture sequences three separate times but I don't yet know their meaning - possibly a code for wire order or action. Need Mute to clarify via a scheme, or you tell me what manual info you have so I can try to correlate.")
wait()
```

Let me think about this differently. Mute is sending gestures to me repeatedly - these must be an attempt at communication since Mute can't speak. The gestures seem to cycle: `☝🖐🤙`, `✌🖐✋`, `🤟🖐☝` repeating across turns. This could be Mute trying to spell something or reference wire numbers/colors using a symbol code they've invented, hoping I can relay meaning back via speech to Blind - even without a shared dictionary, consistent repetition suggests these are stable statements (like "if light X do Y").

Since I can't ask Mute questions (they can't hear me speak... wait, can Mute hear? Let me check: Mute "cannot speak, or touch bomb" - nothing says Mute can't hear. Let me recheck reach table: Deaf cannot hear, Blind and Mute presumably can hear normally since only Deaf is deaf. So Mute CAN hear my speech.

That changes things - I can speak to Mute directly to ask for clarification, and Mute hears me even though they can't respond in speech, only gesture back (which I can see).

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures but have no shared code for them yet. Can you gesture using wire numbers 1, 2, 3 corresponding to symbols, like point up for wire 1, peace for wire 2, fist for wire 3, to tell me which wire to cut? Or gesture a color name mapping. I'll relay to Blind by voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Board update: light orange again, display 0, wires unchanged 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow. Still working out Mute's gesture code.")
wait()
```

Interesting - the third gesture changed from `🤟🖐☝` to `✊🖐☝` when the light changed from orange to green (comparing turn 5 and turn 6). The first two gestures `☝🖐🤙` and `✌🖐✋` stayed the same across turns 4,5,6 regardless of light color changes. This suggests:

- Gesture 1 (`☝🖐🤙`) and Gesture 2 (`✌🖐✋`) might be static rules/info (e.g., wire mappings)
- Gesture 3 changes with light color - likely encoding "current light color" or an instruction conditional on light

Let me hypothesize: middle symbol 🖐 (5 fingers/all) might be a separator. So each gesture is [X, separator, Y].

Turn 4 (light white): third gesture not sent (only 2 gestures arrived)
Turn 5 (light orange): third = 🤟🖐☝
Turn 6 (light green): third = ✊🖐☝

So the last symbol stays ☝ but first symbol changes with light: orange→🤟, green→✊. This looks like light-color-to-symbol mapping! Mute may be telling me "when light is orange, the symbol/action is 🤟" and "when light is green, action is ✊" - possibly indicating which wire or action corresponds to current light state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I notice your third gesture's first symbol changes with the light color - orange gave thumb-rock-horns, green gives fist. Are you signaling an action tied to current light color? If so, continue this pattern turn by turn and I'll relay the mapping to Blind as we gather more light colors.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now green, display 0, wires unchanged 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow. Mute seems to be encoding an action per light color via gesture - orange maps to one symbol, green to another. Still decoding, don't act yet.")

```

Now light is white again, and the third gesture reverted to `🤟🖐☝` - same as when light was orange (turn 5)! Wait, let me recheck: turn 4 white had no third gesture, turn 5 orange had `🤟🖐☝`, turn 6 green had `✊🖐☝`, turn 7 white has `🤟🖐☝`.

Hmm, that breaks my white-hasn't-appeared-before theory unless turn 4's missing third gesture was just a timing/turn-order artifact (Mute's turn 4 message may have been sent before seeing turn 4's light, still reflecting turn 3's green... but turn 3 was green and gave no third gesture either, only two).

Let me reconsider timing: I see Mute's message for round N at the *start* of round N+1 (per turn rules: "whatever you missed reaches you at the start of next round"). So the gestures I see in Turn N were sent by Mute during round N-1, reacting to the board Mute saw in round N-1... but wait Mute doesn't see the board, I do. Actually Mute only reads the manual - Mute has no board info at all except what's fixed in the manual.

So Mute's gestures are NOT reacting to light color - they're static manual content unrelated to my board! The correlation with light color turns may be coincidental. Mute is likely just repeating manual excerpts each turn, and my two options are recurring lines while third rotates through a short manual list.

I should tell Mute what the light actually is, since Mute can't see it, and ask if this affects which manual rule applies.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Reminder: I see the board, you don't. Currently light is white, display 0, wires 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow, unchanged wires all game. Your gestures may be manual content independent of what I see - can you gesture a fixed label for each rule, like a number, so I can match manual rules to board states I report?")
speak(to="blind", text="Light back to white, display 0, wires still 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow. No change in wires this whole game so far.")
wait()
```

New gestures this time, completely different from before! This suggests Mute *did* receive/understand my request and is now trying a new scheme - likely responding to my ask for numbered labels, or reacting to something else entirely.

Let me compare: previous set was `☝🖐🤙`, `✌🖐✋`, `🤟🖐☝` (or `✊🖐☝`). New set: `🤙🖐✌`, `👋🖐🤟`, `🖖🖐☝`.

The last symbol of gesture 3 is still ☝ — consistent element. Otherwise all different. This really does look like Mute is trying various encodings for me, but without an agreed dictionary I can't decode this reliably.

I think the safest approach: establish a simple protocol. I'll define gesture meanings via speech to Mute (since Mute hears me), proposing a wire-cutting code, and ask Mute to gesture back confirmation using that code once I propose numbers/colors mapped to specific symbols.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let's use a fixed code. I will assign: point-up ☝ means wire 1, peace ✌ means wire 2, fist ✊ means wire 3. Thumbs-up 👍 means yes-safe, thumbs-down 👎 means danger. If your manual says something about a specific wire or light color, gesture using only these symbols so I can understand and relay to Blind. For light colors: open-palm 🖐 for white, victory ✌ already used so use claw 🤌 for orange, and OK-sign 👌 for green. Try again next turn with this code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light now orange, display 0, wires still 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow unchanged. Proposing a gesture code to Mute to get actionable info - stand by, don't act yet.")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝]

Excellent! Mute responded using exactly my proposed code! Let's decode using my own mapping:
- 👌 = green (light), ✌ = wire 2
- 🤌 = orange (light), ✊ = wire 3
- 🖐 = white (light), ☝ = wire 1

So this reads as: "When light is green → wire 2. When light is orange → wire 3. When light is white → wire 1."

Current light is green! So according to this rule: cut wire 2 (blue).

But wait, I should double check this is a "cut this wire" instruction and not something else (like "this wire is safe" or "this wire is dangerous"). Given the manual likely tells which wire to cut based on light color, this fits perfectly as an action table.

Let me relay this to Blind now, but also confirm with Mute since this is critical - one wrong move kills everyone.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Got it, using our code: white to right one (wire 1), orange to fist (wire 3), green to peace (wire 2). So current light green means wire 2. Confirm this is the wire to CUT by gesturing thumbs-up 👍 if correct, thumbs-down 👎 if this is instead a wire to AVOID.")
speak(to="blind", text="Critical update: Mute's manual maps light colors to wires - white=wire1, orange=wire3, green=wire2. Light is currently green, so indicated wire is 2 (blue). Waiting on Mute to confirm whether this means CUT or AVOID that wire before you act. Do not cut yet.")
wait()
```
